decisions.summary: Pages worked by feature 250's landed method; tasks closed are 265's own; FR-010's queues and reserved prefixes the one change; tokens.py summary once per page for the closing report.
decisions.why: The spec's 'What this feature is' now says the same: 250's method, FR-010 the one change the GM added on 2026-09-27. The per-page token summary only feeds FR-009's report.

decisions.summary: make reserve KIND=glossary|registry KEY=<key>: flock on the mirror's lock, next = highest + 10 over the mirror, every clone and a ledger, stub written before release; apply_term reserves its glossary prefix with the full entry as the stub; a race test of eight reservations across two clones in four processes.
decisions.why: This is FR-010's allocator: mirror, every clone and the ledger, the claim is the file, and apply-edits takes its prefix from it. The race test is SC-011's.

decisions.summary: new-file-hooks.sh (PreToolUse on Write and Bash) refuses a call that creates a prefixed file in glossary/ or 010-works-cited/ (a Write, a redirect or tee) unless the ledger holds a reservation for that kind, prefix AND key.
decisions.why: Last round's collision is closed. A hand-taken 0950 for another key no longer passes on a prefix another session reserved, because the key must match. Suite case 2 covers exactly this, and 12 of 12 passed on this round's own run. The reach, the two directories FR-010 names, reached by Write and by shell redirect, is FR-010's 'a new file in either directory written without a reservation is refused'. The plan's text is within. The implementation's Bash branch reaches further than the plan says; that is reported to the session as a code defect against this decision, not as a ruling on the plan.

decisions.summary: page-queue.sh clones to .clones/diagram-research-<n>, generates the briefs there with that clone's own brief.py, and runs page-session there; pull-queue.sh pulls back locally and ALWAYS runs make glossary/record/citations after the merge and commits the result. A generated-file conflict takes this side; any other conflict stops for a person, and the re-run rebuilds.
decisions.why: Last round's condition is gone: the rebuild now runs after every pull, clean or not (pull-queue.sh lines after the merge, and test_pull_queue passed on this round's run). A hand conflict exits and names the files. Re-running once it is committed pulls nothing new and then rebuilds, so the regenerated pages are still rebuilt, not merged by hand, as FR-010 asks. The briefs are generated in the queue clone so its check step reads its own commits, and tasks are named '<feature dir>:<Tnn>' so a 265 page ticks 265's task. Both are mechanics FR-010's queues need, not a change to the process.

decisions.summary: Up to three queues: A urban-features; B towns then ways; C river-cities, buildings, then capitals.
decisions.why: FR-010's 'up to three queues' and SC-011's 'at least two at once'. All six pages the spec names are assigned.

decisions.summary: Sweeps FR-003 to FR-005 run here after every queue is pulled back, then FR-008, then T11 (FR-007 over the sweeps, owed pairs, closing report, page-check, done, push).
decisions.why: This is the order the tasks carry. It is unchanged since the last round.
